issues.failure_explanation: Entrywise the equation aZN^T+bNZ+NZN^T=0 reads a z_{s,t+1}+b z_{s+1,t}+z_{s+1,t+1}=0. For two Jordan blocks of equal size 2, the block Z_{ik} with z_{11}=0, z_{12}=1, z_{21}=-a/b and z_{22}=0 satisfies it. It has nonzero entries at s+t=2 and s+t=3, which the stated threshold (zero if s+t>=max=2) would forbid, so the stated rule would force Z_{ik}=0. Example 3.4 itself shows nonzero f_{12}, f_{21} at s+t=3=max{3,2}, so the text and the example disagree. The threshold for off-diagonal blocks is not uniformly 'max'. The displayed form is also a superset: for n_i=3, n_k=2 the equations force z_{21}=-(a/b)z_{12}, so the f_{ij} in Z_{12} are not independent.

issues.failure_explanation: In Case 2 every unit-circle eigenvalue lambda_j is assigned the doubled structure diag(lambda_j I+N, lambda_j I+N), of size 2n_j. This is not forced by H-palindromic structure. Take n=1, P(lambda)=lambda^2+lambda+1, which is H-palindromic with A=1 and Q=1. Its eigenvalues e^{±2πi/3} are distinct, simple and on the unit circle, so J cannot have the stated form. The Gamma_{jj} blocks in (gs-38) and Corollary 3.7(3) are then 2x2 (S_{j1},S_{j2},S_{j3}; Psi_j in C^{2x2}). Theorem 3.9, however, treats the same blocks as n_j x n_j (E_j of order n_j, S_j=Q_j Sigma_j Q_j^H). With these block sizes the sizes of Gamma no longer add up to 2n, so the theorems are mutually inconsistent. The proof of Theorem 3.6 is also omitted ('similar to Theorem 3.5'). The proof of Theorem 3.9 additionally writes S_k^H=epsilon S_k, whereas the definition of S gives S^H=-epsilon S.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the unit-circle block as J_j=lambda_j I_{n_j}+N_{n_j} of size n_j, with sizes summing to 2n. Restate (gs-38) with Gamma_{jj}=S_j in Theta_{(lambda_j,conj(lambda_j),j)} and S_j^H=-epsilon S_j. Make Corollary 3.7(3) and Theorem 3.9 consistent with this, and supply the omitted proof.
issues.overall_effect: Theorems 3.6 and 3.9 and Corollary 3.7(3) are vacuous or inconsistent for H-palindromic polynomials with unit-circle eigenvalues of non-doubled multiplicity. The parametrization of Gamma for the H case is unreliable in general.
issues.title: Unit-circle eigenvalue blocks of H-palindromic polynomials are forced to be doubled; classification is wrong and inconsistent with Theorem 3.9
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained re-derivation of the H-case structure, using the same method as Theorem 3.5. The overall approach and results survive but several statements must be rewritten.

issues.failure_explanation: Q_j is produced by applying Lemma 3.3 (an SVD, with generic complex unitary factors) to the whole 2n_j x 2n_j matrix V_j=diag(V_{j1},V_{j4}). Nothing ensures that these unitary factors are block diagonal with respect to the distinct eigenvalues lambda_j and conj(lambda_j) of J. The commutation (gs-32) is only asserted ('it is easy to see'), and it holds only if P is block-compatible with J. Moreover X_R=XM^{-1} is real because of the special choice of M. The new X~_R=XP^{-1}DM^{-1}, with an arbitrary complex unitary P, is not shown to be real, so the claim that (X~_R,J_R) is a real standard pair, and that Gamma~_R has the form (gs-31), is unsupported. In addition, D is defined with an extra square root, since D_{jj} already contains ^{1/2}. As written, (gs-34) then does not give identity blocks, and in the cases j>r_1 the sizes of D_j and Phi_j do not match.

issues.failure_explanation: Corollary 3.7(1,2) gives Gamma_R for a real Jordan form J_R. In Theorem 4.1, Lambda is a diagonal complex matrix and X is complex. For such Lambda the corollary's general form (e.g. U=[a b; b -a] with b≠0) violates Lambda Gamma=Gamma Lambda^{-star}, because it couples lambda with conj(lambda) instead of with 1/lambda. Theorem 2.2 needs Gamma in S_{(Lambda,star,epsilon)}, which is not guaranteed by 'of the form given by Corollary 3.7'. Further, the problem prescribes the eigenvectors X, but the closing construction parametrises X=YP with Y=[Y_1,Y_1 Xi], i.e. chooses the eigenvectors freely. This does not solve the stated problem for given eigenpairs, and the data would have to satisfy X Gamma X^star=0 itself.
